newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse siesta to end after Flemish fiesta.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse siesta to end after Flemish fiesta.

text.p: A Flemish regional holiday on Friday left the Brussels bourse in limbo and barely able to react to a surge in the dollar to six-year highs against the mark, dealers said.

As the dollar rose to more than 1.77 marks from levels under 1.75 on Thursday, the Brussels bourse moved sideways with the Bel-20 leading share index ending up just 0.23 percent at 2,492.41 points compared with gains of more than one percent in Amsterdam and Frankfurt.
"We had about half the volume we have usually because the rich Flemish people were on holiday," one trader commented.

He predicted that if the dollar stayed firm in New York trade, the bourse would head higher on Monday once end-investors were back. "But the dollar is very volatile...which makes me a little worried," he added.
Brussels bourse volume was again led by trade in non-ferrous metals maker Union Miniere following this week's private placement by controlling shareholder SGB of 24 percent of the company.
Dollar-sensitive UM ended up 20 francs at 3,430 francs and one trader said if the U.S. currency remained firm a return to the pre-placement level of 3,800 francs was now possible.
SGB rose 50 francs to 3,650 after sinking on Thursday from highs reached in the aftermath of the UM news.
The strongest gainer was Kredietbank, up 225 francs, or 1.51 percent, at 15,125 francs.
Electronics firm Barco edged ahead 30 francs to 7,490 despite a mixed reaction to news of a 700 million franc purchase of a Danish communications company.
However, dollar-sensitive issues Delhaize, Bekaert and PetroFina all ended flat to lower despite the currency's rise.
